proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly derives the metathesized series from laghu and names Nepali halũ/halaũ/huluṅo, Hindi harū/haruā and Gujarati haḷvũ. These whole light adjectives match that l/h or lv series, including nasal and final agreement vowels; initial h loss remains a regional comparison. Forms with k belong to the separate kk extension and are not silently merged here.

proposals.evidence: Turner’s lamba family combines the regional lamb-/lām- long series with Maithili namā, documenting an n-initial variant within the family. The western nāmb-/ṇāmb- survey adjectives preserve the matching medial mb and ordinary final agreement. This is a qualified comparative-family assignment: the local n/l alternation is not presented as a fully established regular sound law, and further -la extensions remain excluded.
